chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Sa'id, from Wasil, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, what do you say about these people who are killed in these frontiers (thughur)?' He said, 'Woe to them! They hasten to a death in the world and a death in the Hereafter. And by God, the martyr is none of us, even if they die on their beds.'

key_terms.الثُّغُور: Frontier regions or borderlands where battles take place
key_terms.الْوَيْلُ: Woe or destruction (a warning of punishment)
key_terms.فُرُشِهِمْ: Their beds (symbolizing dying in comfort or without specific religious intent)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a general martyr and a true Shi'a according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general concept of martyrdom (*shahada*) and the specific theological status of being 'Shi'a' (followers of the Ahl al-Bayt). He warns that those who fight in the frontier wars (*thughur*) for worldly motives or general striving, without allegiance to the Imams, hasten to a 'death in the Hereafter'—a state of spiritual loss—emphasizing that true Shi'ah identity is rooted in loyalty to the Prophet's household rather than merely the act of dying in battle.
